# The Visualization Coordinator {#sec-tech-visualization}

`app/view/visualization.R` hosts a navset with a permanent **New plot** tab (the
creator form) plus one tab per live plot. Each plot tab is an instance of
`app/view/visualization_plot.R` that owns its own setup sidebar and its own engine
submodule server:

```{.r filename="app/view/visualization.R"}
# Visualization coordinator. Hosts a navset of plot tabs: a permanent "New plot"
# tab carrying the creator form, plus one tab per live plot. Each plot tab is an
# app/view/visualization_plot.R instance that owns its own setup sidebar and its
# own engine submodule server, so several plots — including several of the same
# type — run independently ...
```

## The multi-tab model {#sec-tech-viz-tabs}

`visualization_plot.R` holds the registry that binds a plot type to its engine
module, its distance requirement and its export route:

```{.r filename="app/view/visualization_plot.R"}
MST  = list(mod = visualization_mst,  distance = TRUE,  export_kind = "widget"),
Tree = list(mod = visualization_tree, distance = TRUE,  export_kind = "ggplot"),
Map  = list(mod = visualization_map,  distance = FALSE, export_kind = "widget"),
Epi  = list(mod = visualization_epi,  distance = FALSE, export_kind = "ggplot"),
AMR  = list(mod = visualization_amr,  distance = FALSE, export_kind = "ggplot")
```

::: {.callout-important title="Plot type is fixed for a tab's lifetime"}
The plot type is chosen on the New-plot form and never changes for that tab — it
is a plain character scalar, not a reactive. Nothing downstream may assume it can
change: the type decides both which controls the sidebar emits and which of the
five engine submodules is instantiated. This is what lets the coordinator run five
different engines through one tab abstraction without them interfering.
:::

What stays in the coordinator is only what is genuinely shared: the cached
per-isolate metadata read (the `store`, @sec-arch-signals), the staged import sets
(@sec-tech-interop-staging), the Save picker's grouped choices, the page-level
scripts that must be registered exactly once (including the high-resolution export
capture, @sec-tech-viz-export), and the tab registry itself — create, close,
teardown, and the dashboard's Add Plot / open-saved-plot hand-offs
(@sec-tech-dashboard).

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-tech-viz
%%| fig-cap: "The visualization workspace: one coordinator, one visualization_plot instance per open tab, one of five engine servers per instance."
flowchart TD
  C["visualization.R<br/><i>coordinator · shared store · tab registry</i>"]
  C --> NP["New plot tab<br/>(creator form)"]
  C -- "1 per open tab" --> T1["visualization_plot"]
  C -- "1 per open tab" --> T2["visualization_plot"]
  T1 --> E1["exactly one engine server:<br/>visualization_mst · _tree · _epi · _map · _amr"]
  T2 --> E2["exactly one engine server"]
```

## Compute once, draw many times {#sec-tech-viz-generate}

Every distance-based engine follows the same performance split: the **expensive**
step (reading profiles, building the distance matrix, computing the tree/MST) runs
only when the user presses **Generate**; the **cheap** steps (colour, layout,
labels) redraw live as controls change. The logic modules embody this split —
`phylo.R` computes, `mst_plot.R`/`tree_plot.R` draw — so a control change never
recomputes a distance matrix (@sec-tech-engines).

## Mapping variables to aesthetics {#sec-tech-viz-mapping}

`app/logic/mapping_engine.R` decides which aesthetic a chosen variable is drawn
onto, from the variable's profile and from what the other layers already occupy:

```{.r filename="app/logic/mapping_engine.R"}
# Here the user picks the *variable* and this module picks the rest, from the
# variable's profile (app/logic/field_profile.R) and from what the other layers
# already occupy. Every rule below is a rule about legibility, and each one names
# the failure it exists to prevent.
```

::: {.callout-important title="Each rule names the failure it prevents"}
A 46-level variable sent to a colour-brewer palette drew nine categories in colour
and the rest in grey; a variable with more than six levels sent to *shape* had its
surplus categories vanish from the plot. Both failed **silently**. The rules — "a
shape cannot show a continuum", "a tabulated palette cannot show 46 countries" —
exist to make those states unreachable. `eligible_aesthetics()`,
`assign_mapping_layer()` and `rebalance_layers()` implement the ranking, and the
same rules serve both media: a **tree** draws onto tip points, labels and tile
strips; an **MST** draws onto node fill alone (a merged node's pie is the one
channel that can show all its members' values). A new engine adds its medium to
`MAPPING_MEDIA` rather than inventing its own selection logic.
:::

## Exporting a plot {#sec-tech-viz-export}

`app/logic/viz_export.R` owns the shared **Export Plot** panel and the
size/resolution arithmetic behind every format. Two export routes, distinguished
by the `kind` argument:

- **`ggplot`** (Tree, Epi, AMR) — the plot object lives on the server, so export
  re-renders it at the requested physical size and DPI. A vector PDF/SVG has no
  resolution to lose, and a raster is drawn at the requested DPI, not scraped off
  the screen (`save_plot_export()`, `resolved_dpi()`).
- **`widget`** (MST, Map) — drawn by the browser, so the image must come back from
  the client. The capture is **not** a screenshot: `visualization.R`'s
  `phylotrace_capture` handler makes the widget redraw itself into a larger buffer
  first, so a 4× export is a genuine re-render at four times the linear resolution
  (`write_data_uri()`). Both widget engines also offer self-contained interactive
  HTML.

## Saving to the dashboard {#sec-tech-viz-save}

Each plot tab can save its full input snapshot (plus a thumbnail) into an Analysis
in the loaded database. The coordinator builds the grouped Save picker and routes
the two dashboard hand-offs — "Add Plot" for an Analysis and "open a saved plot" —
into preselecting or restoring the right tab (@sec-tech-dashboard). The
persistence lives in `app/logic/analysis_store.R`, inside the `.db` itself.

## Chapter summary

- One coordinator, one `visualization_plot` instance per tab, one engine server
  per instance; the type/engine binding lives in `plot_type_meta`.
- Plot type is fixed per tab and is not a reactive.
- Distance engines compute on Generate and redraw cheaply on control changes.
- `mapping_engine.R` centralizes aesthetic selection; every rule in it prevents a
  specific silent-failure mode.
- `viz_export.R` exports ggplot engines by server re-render and widget engines by
  a genuine high-resolution client redraw.
